Last year, Apple brought a radical multitasking overhaul to the iPad with iPadOS 26, introducing windowed mode. Initially, the simpler multitasking modes — Split View and Slide Over — were removed. Those features did eventually return, but only if you opted into that new, clunky windowing system. I was hopeful iPadOS 27 would improve the situation, but sadly that wasn't the case.

To be clear, I'm not entirely against the new windowing system in iPadOS 26 (now 27). It has its place, and when I'm using a 13-inch iPad Pro with a Magic Keyboard juggling multiple apps, it works brilliantly. For smaller iPads, I'm more split, but it's generally fine.

What I don't like, though, is that beyond Stage Manager (which I see more as a feature within the windowing system than a separate option), the only choice is full-screen for every app — with zero flexibility.

What I was hoping to see

As mentioned, iPadOS 26 eventually reintroduced Split View and Slide Over in a later beta — but only if you have windowed mode enabled. That means if you want simpler multitasking, you're forced to contend with a layer of complexity designed for power users.

That's not inherently a problem, of course, but it can be genuinely annoying to have to wrestle a window into just the right position to snap into Split View or Slide Over, and it's nowhere near as seamless as it was before iPadOS 26. It's also a loss for those who like windowed mode, because accidentally nudging a window slightly off-axis can trigger Split Over when that's not what you wanted.

Apple does give you the option to long-press the red, yellow, or green circles to switch more precisely between Split View and Slide Over states, but that's hardly an intuitive gesture for everyday iPad use.

Split View and Slide Over should be part of iPadOS, but stuffing them inside the windowing system makes them more cumbersome than they need to be — even after a year.

The takeaway

Ideally, iPadOS would offer two multitasking modes: Classic and Pro. Classic would essentially be full-screen apps with Slide Over and Split View as options; Pro would be the windowing system introduced in iPadOS 26. Within Pro, there should also be the option to toggle Stage Manager on or off.

G A B E 🪐's top comments

What frustrates me is that Slide Over hasn't really returned in any meaningful way. Unless I have a Magic Keyboard folio attached or an external display plugged in, I have zero interest in Stage Manager (side note: it would be great if the iPad automatically entered Stage Manager mode when one of these accessories is connected). I'm very curious to see how the folding iPhone handles multitasking.

Overall, I think Apple has pushed the iPad too far in one direction, catering primarily to Magic Keyboard or laptop replacement users, while making the multitasking experience worse for those who want to use their iPad as an iPad. Adding a 'simple' multitasking option would go a long way toward fixing this.

What do you think of the iPad multitasking experience since iPadOS 26? Let me know in the comments.
